# A two-limb number equal to a limb

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/Statements.v, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `eq_2_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Whether $x = a$, for the exact values:

$$m = [\, x = a \,].$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x == a` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | `bool` |  |
| `a == x` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` |  |
| `x != a` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | `bool` | the negation of `x == a` |
| `a != x` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `bool` | the negation of `a == x` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $m$ is true exactly when $x = a$, for the exact values.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit and any exponent range, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `eq_2_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Compare.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Compare.v), against `eq_2_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition eq_2_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 a : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  let m := eq_2_1 x0 x1 a in
  m = Req_bool (x0 + x1) a.
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** limbs compared in order (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/eq_2_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/eq_2_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`, rounded to nearest; `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# x = a: eq_2_2 with (a, 0) in place of y. Equality is symmetric, so there is no eq_1_2.

h = eq(x0, a)
l = eq(x1, 0)
m = and(h, l)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#eq_2_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 65 600 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 65 600 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 12 858 634 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
